response: Yes, the outcome of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in children with malignancy can be predicted to some extent. According to research, peak inspiratory pressure, PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure), and ventilation index values can distinguish survivors from nonsurvivors by day 3. This means that by monitoring these values, healthcare providers may be able to identify children who are at higher risk of poor outcomes and provide early intervention with supportive nonconventional therapies, potentially improving their chances of survival.
